title: The mechanosensitive channel TMEM63B contributes to noxious heat sensation in the dorsal root ganglia
abstract:
by Chang Ye, Yan-Yu Zang, Gui-Fang Duan, Jiang Chen, Dan Wu, Dan Wang, Changlin Li, Yun Xu, Tianjiao Xia, Xiaoping Gu, Yun Stone Shi

In mammals, heat sensation is primarily mediated by thermosensitive channels, particularly transient receptor potential (TRP) channels, in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons. However, whether additional channels contribute to noxious heat detection remains unclear. Here, we investigated the role of the mechanosensitive cation channel TMEM63B in DRG neurons and unexpectedly discovered its involvement in noxious thermosensation rather than mechanosensation. TMEM63B was broadly expressed in DRG neurons, and its global knockout or DRG-specific conditional knockout markedly reduced heat sensitivity. Deletion of TMEM63B significantly attenuated heat-induced calcium responses and currents in DRG neurons and elevated the temperature threshold for action potential initiation. title: PrimeStack editors enable efficient and site-specific integration of large multigene cargos in plants
abstract:
by Edith Sánchez, Khalid Sedeek, Haroon Butt, Magdy Mahfouz

Precise, site-specific integration of large DNA sequences into plant genomes is a long-standing goal of crop biotechnology and synthetic biology, yet remains constrained by random insertion, inefficient homologous recombination, and gene targeting. Here, we present PrimeStack, a DSB-independent platform that integrates PE with the unidirectional large serine integrase Bxb1, leveraging evolved variants for enhanced activity, to achieve the programmable insertion of multigene, multikilobase cargos at predefined genomic safe harbors (GSH) in rice (Oryza sativa). Optimized prime editors first install attP landing sites with high fidelity and heritability followed by Bxb1-mediated recombination that generates irreversible integration of genetic information. title: The hidden challenges of return migration: Linguistic and academic re-adaptation of Syrian students to the Arabic Education System
abstract:
by Sevda Dolapcioglu, Yunus Emre Akbana, İlayda Uzun, Gülten Koşar

While extensive research has examined refugee students’ educational adaptation in host countries, the educational reintegration phase following voluntary return remains underexplored. This qualitative study investigates the linguistic and academic adaptation experiences of Syrian students transitioning from Turkish-medium education in Türkiye to Arabic-medium schooling in Syria after voluntary return. The study addresses an overarching question: how do returnee students experience the linguistic, academic, social, and psychosocial dimensions of this reverse educational transition? Using an exploratory qualitative design, data were collected through a seven-item open-ended written questionnaire from 15 middle-school students who had received several years of formal schooling in Türkiye. title: The double-edged sword of human-AI collaboration on design students’ competence development: The mediating roles of challenge and hindrance appraisals and the asymmetric moderation of teacher AI leadership
abstract:
by Xiang Wang, MingXing Li, Jia Du, YU Yao, Jiabei Jiang

The deepening integration of generative AI into design education is driving a paradigm shift in human-computer AI collaboration (HAIC) -from mere tool assistance toward intelligent synergy. However, its dual impact on the competency development of design students and the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Grounded in the Theory of Stress Appraisal, this study constructs a research model to examine the double-edged sword effect of HAIC on Design Competence (DC), introducing teacher AI Leadership (AIL) as a moderating variable. The aim is to reveal the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions through which HAIC influences DC. Employing a questionnaire survey, this study conducted an empirical investigation involving 483 design students in East China. Agrobacterium-mediated transient expression has revolutionised plant research, enabling numerous landmark discoveries across diverse areas of plant biology. Yet this powerful approach remains largely confined to solanaceous species, leaving most economically important crop families without a comparable rapid assay platform. Here, we show that an engineered Rhizobium rhizogenes strain, AS109, mediates efficient transient expression across diverse dicot species spanning multiple taxonomic families, consistently outperforming commonly used laboratory agrobacterial strains. title: Deficiency of placental GDF15 causes fetal growth restriction by inhibiting fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 axis
abstract:
by Xiao Peng Liu, Xiao Zhang, Chun Xia Cai, Miao Miao Qin, Xiang Kai Leng, Jia Hao Chen, Yi Fan Han, Jun Ying Xiao, Jia He Huang, Jiang Wei Wu

Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality, yet its underlying mechanism remains elusive. Here, we show that growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) levels are significantly reduced in the placenta and fetal circulation in mouse and pig FGR models and correlate positively with fetal weight. Placenta-specific GDF15 deficiency causes FGR, while placenta-specific Gdf15 mRNA delivery through targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) effectively alleviates FGR. Mechanistically, placental GDF15 is a major contributor to the fetal circulating GDF15 pool and enters the fetal compartment, where it activates the hepatic STAT3 signaling pathway to stimulate IGF2 production during pregnancy. Background

Education outcomes are associated with life chances. However, deprivation, ill-health and disability are barriers to achievement. We aimed to investigate educational attainment of children with and without major congenital anomalies in state-funded mainstream schools at ages 11 and 16 (key stages [KS] 2 and 4), accounting for maternal and child socioeconomic deprivation, demographic factors, comorbidities, and special education needs (SEN) provision.

title: Meta reinforcement learning for robust quadruped locomotion under joint failures
abstract:
by Likai Wu, Chee-Onn Chow, Wei Ru Wong, Joon Huang Chuah, Jeevan Kanesan, Meina Zhang

Joint failures can disrupt gait coordination, velocity tracking, and body stability in quadruped robots by reducing the available control authority. This study investigates faults in which joints remain locked at fixed angles and presents Adjudicate Reconfiguration and Evolving Regularization Meta Reinforcement Learning (ARER-MetaRL). The framework combines task inference from context, modular routing tailored to each task through an Adjudicate Reconfiguration (AR) network, and Evolving Gradient Regularization (ER) to support rapid adaptation. Tasks differ in the identities and locking angles of the faulty joints, the number of simultaneous faults, the commanded motion direction, and the terrain. title: Rates of nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) regression among patients with very mild or mild NPDR in an Indian Health Service teleophthalmology program, 2015 – 2020
abstract:
by Sven-Erik Bursell, Stephanie J. Fonda, Kaitlynn Borik, Jeff Stainback, Dara Shahon

Diabetic retinopathy (DR) regression is not regularly reported; yet understanding of its prevalence in early-stage DR may impact strategies for eye care management. This study’s primary aim was to examine DR regression in patients initially diagnosed with very mild or mild nonproliferative DR (NPDR). A secondary aim was to assess the association between retinopathy regression and diabetes therapy, diabetes duration, and Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c). This was a retrospective, longitudinal cohort study using medical record data from the United States’s Indian Health Service’s teleophthalmology program for DR evaluation. Baseline exams occurred in 2015–2017 and follow-up (FU) exams occurred within 3 years of baseline. title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78716-1

Despite numerous studies on solid-state high-harmonic generation (HHG), there is a lack of microscopic understanding of decoherence effects. Here, the authors study experimentally and by real-time ab-initio simulations the wavelength dependence of HHG in monolayer films, promoting momentum-resolved electron-phonon scattering as the dominant many-body interaction causing ultrafast decoherence.

title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11150-x

Longitudinal genomic analyses in patients with astrocytoma or oligodendrioglioma suggest that these two types of tumour differ in the mechanisms by which they become resistant to treatment, with astrocytomas accumulating copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability markers but oligodendrogliomas acquiring new driver mutations.

title: Syntaxin11 deficiency inhibits CRAC channel priming to suppress cytotoxicity and gene expression in T lymphocytes independent of membrane trafficking
abstract: Mutations in Syntaxin11 (STX11), a Q-SNARE, result in a fatal immune disorder known as familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis 4 (FHLH4) in human patients. A key diagnostic feature of FHLH4 is defective T and natural killer cell cytotoxicity. Here, we show that STX11 directly binds and regulates Orai1, the pore-forming subunit of calcium release-activated calcium (CRAC) channels. CRAC channels enable store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) from the extracellular space and are crucial for granule exocytosis and nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT)-dependent gene expression in activated lymphocytes. STX11 depletion strongly inhibited SOCE, CRAC currents, NFAT activation, interleukin-2 gene expression, and degranulation in FHLH4 patient T lymphocytes and cell lines without affecting membrane trafficking. title: Bruce suppresses autophagy-regulated caspase activity and wing tissue growth in Drosophila
abstract: Caspases are cysteine-aspartic proteases that mediate both lethal and non-lethal cellular outcomes, including the promotion of tissue growth. However, the mechanisms underlying the differential regulation of these activities remain unclear. We have previously shown that among the two Drosophila executioner caspases, Dcp-1 and Drice, Dcp-1 promotes tissue growth in a non-lethal manner, independent of canonical apoptotic signaling. Herein, we demonstrated that overexpressed Dcp-1, but not Drice, was activated without canonical apoptosome components. TurboID-based proximity labeling revealed distinct proximal proteomes, among which Sirtuin 1, an Atg8a deacetylase, which promotes autophagy, was specifically required for Dcp-1 activation. Autophagy-related genes, including Bcl-2 family members Debcl and Buffy, are required for Dcp-1 activation. title: Separable downmodulation of meiotic axis protein deposition and DNA break induction at chromosome ends
abstract: In many organisms, meiotic crossover recombination is suppressed near the extreme ends of chromosomes. Here, we show that multiple, often chromosome-specific, suppressive mechanisms with differing ranges contribute to the consistently low enrichment of recombination-promoting axis proteins and the downregulation of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within 20 kb of telomeres in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Suppression of axis proteins is associated with cis-encoded signals and correlates with reduced coding density, although whether this sequence feature actively drives suppression remains to be determined. In addition, axis protein suppression requires the histone methyltransferase Dot1 and the Sir silencing complex. We show that Dot1 suppresses Sir complex activity at least in part independently of its canonical target, H3K79, to downmodulate axis protein deposition near chromosome ends. title: Individual dopaminergic neurons induce unique, yet overlapping combinations of behavioural modulations, including safety learning, memory retrieval, and acute locomotion
abstract: Two evolutionary highly conserved functions of dopamine are to carry ‘teaching’ signals during associative learning and to control movement. In mammals and humans, these functions are generally thought to be produced by different populations of neurons. Here, we investigated in the larva of Drosophila melanogaster whether both these functions can be induced by the same individual dopaminergic neurons in the central brain. Focusing on the dopaminergic neurons of the DL1 cluster, we asked whether the optogenetic activation of individual neurons established associative punishment and/or safety memories, controlled the retrieval of the established memories, and acutely modulated locomotion. We found that each neuron had a unique yet overlapping set of behavioural effects. title: Associations of food processing and dietary risk factors with colorectal cancer incidence in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study: A cohort study
abstract:

Background

Ultra-processed foods (UPF) account for >50% of energy intake by US adults. UPF intake can include dietary components linked to lower colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, such as whole grain and dairy products, and others linked to higher CRC risk, such as processed meats, potentially explaining the heterogeneity of evidence for an association between UPF and CRC risk. Background

Given emerging evidence on the waning of immunity from typhoid conjugate vaccines (TCV), the World Health Organization (WHO) commissioned a multi-model comparison to determine the optimal schedule in terms of health and economic impact to inform updated recommendations for TCV use across different settings.

To identify optimal vaccination strategies across different incidence settings and vaccine waning assumptions, we compared two agent-based and two compartmental dynamic models of typhoid transmission. Background
